newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INTERVIEW - Dutch Content targets foreign expansion.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Dutch Content targets foreign expansion.

text.p: Dutch temporary employment agency Content Beheer sees expansion abroad as a response to slower growth in the Dutch market, chief executive officer Sylvia Toth said on Monday.
"We are only a small player in Europe...we are very actively seeking acquisition possibilities in Germany and Spain," Toth told Reuters in an interview.
She added Content was also looking at expansion options in the United States, as well as in the Netherlands.
Turnover of the Dutch temp market surged 24 percent in 1996, but with all of its income coming from the Netherlands, Content seems relatively vulnerable to the expected slowdown.
"Growth of the Dutch temp market will slow down to an annual rate of 10 to 15 percent, but temps are gaining importance within companies' staffing policies," Toth said.
"We are very dependent on the Netherlands, but foreign expansion might reduce this," she added.
Content has been on the outlook for acquisitions for several years already, but until now has not succeeded in finding a perfect match.
"Any acquisition we make has to be a strategic fit, contribute to earnings per share from day one and fit perfectly with the company culture," Toth said.
Toth said acquisitions of up to around 180 million guilders could be financed without issuing additional shares, but a share issue was be possible in the case of a bigger buy.
She said she was also not opposed to Content becoming part of an international alliance.
"Content is permanently being approached by other players. If a good international combination can be forged, in which we could preserve our own identity, I would not say no," Toth said.
"For the moment, we're doing perfectly well on our own, but you have to be realistic. We would seriously consider such an offer," she said.
Toth said Content intended to boost its turnover from 380.8 million guilders in 1996 to an annual 700 milion guilders by the year 2000.
Apart from acquisitions, Content's growth should come from an increased number of branches, a doubling of turnover in company training by 2000 and expansion of its call centre business.
Toth said Content planned to open at least 10 outlets a year. In 1996, it had 76 branches.
Content's provision of trained administrative personnel accounts for 55 to 60 perent of turnover and will remain the company's core activity, she said.
Toth said she did not expect Content's operating margin -- 7.0 percent in 1996 -- to slip due to the internationalisation of the business.
"We are active in a high-margin niche, and although we sometimes have to compromise on price, I don't expect our margins seriously to come under pressure," she said.
Call centres are currently booming, she said.
"The demand for call centres is explosive," said Toth, adding the annual growth rate of the sector of up to 50 percent mentioned in a Goldman Sachs report in May seemed realistic.
"But I can't guarantee we'll grow at that rate," she said.
-- Christine Lucassen, Amsterdam newsroom 31-20-504 5000
